conviction_note: The reported quarter looks pre-signalled inside the guide: Q3 same-store sales were tracking above 3% on 9 Sep, with about 10 of 13 weeks done, against a 3-4% guide. The move therefore turns on the Q4/FY guide into a weak sector tape: Domino's US comps were +0.3%, dining visits -2.4% in August, CPI 3.7%. Against that sits a stock 25% below its IPO price, sell-side targets cut through October, and short interest near a quarter of the true public float. The evidence nets to a slight long tilt (p_up 53) on a large unsigned move (10.5, near the 11.3% event-implied move). impact_sum (+1.0) and the scaled number (+0.63) agree in sign.
bar: Company guide from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000212704326000008/q22026earningsrelease.htm, 2026-09-09): Q3 SSS +3.0-4.0%, Q3 adj EBITDA growth >=13%; FY26 SSS +2.5-3.0%, NUG >=8%, adj EBITDA growth >=20%. No revenue guide. The sell-side consensus is unresolved: Benzinga shows Q3 EPS $0.08 / revenue $208.6M (the revenue equals the Q2 actual, so it is probably mislabelled), and Stocktwits shows EPS $0.15. Sizes are anchored on the company guide only.
positioning_check: MarketBeat (Last Record Date 2026-10-15, FINRA publication 2026-10-26, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/JMKE/short-interest/): 11,184,307 shares short, 3.7 days to cover, 3.52% 'of float'. That denominator is about 318M total shares. The true public float is the 43.5M IPO shares (up to ~50M with the greenshoe) per the IPO dealcard (https://www.rwbaird.com/transactions/investment-banking/dealcard/6758/), so short is roughly 22-26% of the shares that actually trade (my arithmetic). Baseline: 25d skew +9.69 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.35, event-implied move 11.29%, spot 17.26 = -29% from the 52w high, +7% from the low, -25% vs the $23 IPO price, 5d run-up -3.1%.

findings.finding: On the 9 Sep Q2 call management said Q3 same-store sales were 'tracking above 3%' quarter-to-date, against a Q3 guide of 3.0-4.0%. Q3 ends about 27 Sep (Q2 ended 28 Jun), so about 10 of 13 weeks were already in. The Q3 comp should therefore land inside the guide, most likely in the low-to-mid 3s, and the market was told to expect it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior print (Q2, 2026-09-09): SSS +2.3% with an accelerating QTD and a 3-4% Q3 guide bought +7.44%. Only one observation, so it is not a base rate.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is in the wire. If the market doubted it, sell-side previews would sit below 3%, and none found does. It is the residual small upside from a likely mid-range print after a 23% drawdown.
findings.independence: Same QTD statement in the company's Q2 8-K ('acceleration has continued into the third quarter'), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002127043/000212704326000008/q22026earningsrelease.htm. That is the same speaker, so not independent.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after JMKE last spoke point to a weak QSR consumer into Q4. Domino's US SSS was +0.3% for Q3 against ~0.7% expected (8-K, 13 Oct), with the guide at the low end of low-single digits. Placer.ai dining-chain visits were -2.4% YoY in August. September CPI was 3.7% with gasoline above $4. JMKE's FY SSS guide of 2.5-3.0% (Q1 1.7%, Q2 2.3%, Q3 ~3.5%) implies a Q4 comp of roughly 3-4.5%, which is at risk of being trimmed or held only at the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior guide cut as a public company. On the one prior print, the forward guide (3-4% Q3 comp) was the line bought +7.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell from ~22.4 after Q2 to 17.26, and 25d skew is +9.7 for puts. It is filed because no company-level confirmation of October trends exists; if the market had fully priced a guide cut, targets would have been cut toward spot. The lowest target is $22, still 27% above spot.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. Same direction: Placer.ai/CPI cited in https://www.webull.com/news/15747808216507392 (2026-10-14), and Chipotle downgraded by TD Cowen on traffic, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/21/chipotle-falls-5-as-td-cowen-downgrades-cuts-target-to-32-mcdonalds-and-yum-brands-slip/. Against: JMKE said on its Q2 call that it was outperforming fast-casual traffic; that caveat is already in the reduced size.

findings.finding: The sell-side has pre-cut the bar since the Q2 print. JPMorgan and Jefferies cut targets $26->$24 (29 Sep), TD Cowen $26->$22 (7 Oct), Raymond James $29->$26 (16 Oct); consensus target fell from $28.52 to $27.78 in a month. Expectations into the print have been reset lower while ratings stayed Buy.
findings.why_not_priced: Target cuts are public. The point is that they lower the bar a mid-range print has to clear. If it were fully priced, previews would still be calling for a beat-and-raise and the stock would not be 25% under its IPO price.
findings.independence: Shares a theme with finding 2 (sector weakness is the likely reason for the cuts) but is a different object: the sell-side bar, not the consumer data. No separate URL.

findings.finding: Short interest is 11.18M shares (3.7 days to cover, settlement 15 Oct). MarketBeat calls that 3.52% of float, but only ~43.5-50M Class A shares were sold in the IPO, with Blackstone holding the rest, so roughly 22-26% of the actually traded float is short into a print the company pre-signalled as in-guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print, with SSS acceleration and an in-line guide, gapped +7.4%; the short position then was unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators print 3.5%, which reads as uncrowded. Measured against the real public float it is crowded. If the market had read it that way, the 25d skew would not be +9.7 vol points toward puts; the put/call OI of 0.35 does show call-heavy open interest, so positioning is mixed rather than one-sided.
findings.independence: Float denominator from the IPO size, https://www.rwbaird.com/transactions/investment-banking/dealcard/6758/ (43,478,261 shares at $23). The ratio is my arithmetic, not a published figure.

findings.finding: Q3 adj EBITDA guide of >=13% looks conservative. Q2 adj EBITDA grew 7% but ~18% ex a $10M ad-fund timing gap, and the $8M annualising saving from the area-director buyout continues. The FY >=20% guide also needs H2 well above 13%. An EBITDA print in the high teens is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One print: Q2 EBITDA +7% headline (+18% underlying) bought +7.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide floor is public, but the ad-fund timing makes the quarterly EBITDA hard to model; consensus likely sits near the 13% floor. It lands inside what the company guided (>=), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Ad-fund timing and underlying-18% detail in the call summary, https://reportify.cn/news/1295218541548802048, the same company source.

outside_window.finding: The 180-day IPO lock-up ends about 2027-01-26 (aggregator, single source); Blackstone holds most of the shares, so supply overhang lands after the window.

baseline_tension: Downside skew and the 23% post-Q2 drawdown agree with the sector-weakness finding, which is therefore mostly priced. The in-guide Q3, the lowered sell-side bar and a short that is crowded against the real float cut against the skew, hence only a mild long tilt.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): Q3 SSS finding +0.5 -> +0.3 and EBITDA finding +0.5 -> +0.3, because both land inside what the company already guided.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): macro/guide-risk finding -1.0 -> -0.7. It also agrees with the +9.7 put skew, so it is largely priced.
Rule 5 (positioning is not a document): sell-side target-cut finding +0.5 -> +0.3; short-interest finding +1.0 -> +0.8 because the true-float ratio is my arithmetic.
Rule 8 / core 3b: abs_move_pct kept at 10.5, near the 11.3 event-implied move, not shrunk; p_up 52 -> 53 after re-reading the squeeze mechanism.
